requirements.requirement: Run a healthy background worker managed as inventory-worker under the dedicated unprivileged inventorysvc account.
requirements.summary: The enabled service was active and its heartbeat advanced. Its process ran as UID/GID 996, with no effective capabilities and NoNewPrivileges enabled. The same healthy state was observed after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Confine the worker to a root-owned chroot in which /var/lib/inventory is its only writable application directory.
requirements.summary: The chroot and its non-state directories were root-owned. Direct namespace evidence showed the chroot root mounted read-only and /var/lib/inventory mounted read-write; unprivileged checks denied writes elsewhere. The policy remained effective after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after implementation and reboot, the node remained RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64. The implementation used existing platform binaries, and final package health remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The independent node-restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, the reboot was acknowledged and observed through loss of connectivity, the post-restart boot ID differed, and the enabled service, confinement, heartbeat, and persistent start counter recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: No full package transaction history was captured, although the complete command trace contains no package-management mutation and the final package-health check passed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Final hygiene was clean: no failed units, added network listeners, temporary residue, or package damage were observed. Two bounded implementation mistakes caused unnecessary transient mutations: the initial library copy preserved an unusable libtinfo symlink and was fully repaired by replacing copied libraries (cmd-3e9cb505cc7a489c, cmd-6dfd1052bebb4477); the first service unit used an ineffective ReadWritePaths value, briefly causing worker write errors, and was fully corrected before final verification (cmd-5a41a4c8db0f4700, cmd-69a4b2d8097d4bc8). Neither remained after completion.
